subject: Nanotechnology
title: DNA Nanotech in Drug Delivery
description: A quick win: understand DNA Nanotech in Drug Delivery.

hook.text: A DNA origami barrel that carries doxorubicin to tumor cells and releases it only when it senses the target — precision medicine.

buildup.text: Doxorubicin intercalates between DNA base pairs — the origami itself becomes the drug carrier without extra packaging.

discovery.text: Aptamer locks on the barrel recognize cell-surface markers — the barrel opens only at tumor cells, sparing healthy tissue.

twist.text: DNA is degraded by nucleases in the blood — protective coatings or chemical modifications are needed for in vivo survival.

climax.text: Animal studies show DNA origami improving tumor targeting and reducing side effects — clinical trials are on the horizon.

punchline.text: DNA delivers drugs with an address label — smart packages for smart medicine.

quiz.question: How does doxorubicin bind to DNA origami drug carriers?
options: It is chemically bonded to the surface of the origami through covalent links
It intercalates between DNA base pairs, using the origami structure itself as the carrier
It is encapsulated inside a lipid coating around the origami
